headline: Oversold chips bounce and Amazon jumps 5%, lifting the Nasdaq 1.1% while most stocks fall
summary: A narrow, tech-only rebound. The Nasdaq opened about 1% higher and held the gain all day, while the S&P 500 peaked near 7,731 before fading into the close. Under the surface most stocks fell: NYSE decliners beat advancers about 1.7 to 1, seven of 11 S&P sectors closed lower, and the Dow slipped after swinging around unchanged.
drivers: Chips snap a record losing run

The SOX rose 1.6%, ending an eight-day slide of about 15.7%, its longest since 2008, as bargain hunters returned after the heaviest hedge-fund tech selling on Goldman's records. Intel +2.4% on a JPMorgan upgrade to neutral; Nvidia gained about 2%, and memory names (Micron, Sandisk) led early gains.
Amazon and Tesla carry consumer stocks

Amazon rose 5% after Morgan Stanley named it a top pick and Tesla added 3.8% ahead of Wednesday's results, so consumer discretionary (+2.7%) was the best sector. Cleveland-Cliffs jumped 16% on a third-quarter profit beat.

CoreWeave gave back an early pop from a Goldman upgrade to buy and closed down 0.4% after last week's 25% drop on its roughly $50B debt load; Nebius (+2.9%) and IREN (+2.7%) did better. Traders called the day an oversold bounce rather than a change in the AI-financing worries.

The 10-year yield rose about 4bp to 5.14% as global bond yields climbed with protests in France and Italy, and homebuilder confidence fell to 29, a 14-year low. Utilities (−2%) and real estate (−1.2%) were the worst sectors; JPMorgan, Visa and Sherwin-Williams weighed on the Dow.
week: Week so far: Nasdaq +1.1%, S&P 500 +0.4%, Dow −0.1%, a partial bounce after last week's 4.5% Nasdaq drop. Oil stayed volatile: the expiring November WTI contract rose 2.2% on renewed Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities, while the December contract slipped 0.5% after the US waived some Russia sanctions.
watch: Next: SpaceX reports Tuesday, Meta and Tesla on Wednesday, with Lam Research and Texas Instruments later in the week; the Fed meets next week with September CPI at 3.7%.
